words: Stenger argues logical conclusions inherit their premises’ weakness, whereas physical reasons permit complexity from simpler states, challenging theistic coherence and cumulative evidence to establish divine necessity.
critique: Strongest feature: Stenger joins premise quality to explanatory force, contrasting theological starting points with physical reasons for complexity arising from simpler states, directly answering both the coherence defense and cumulative case. Principal limitation: The excerpt asserts a natural tendency and very good physical reason without specifying a physical mechanism, observation, or model, so evidence warrant and charitable calibration remain weaker than contact with the opposing claims. Live burden: The reply must identify which theistic premises fail and develop the physical account enough to show natural emergence undercuts divine necessity, not merely offers another possibility. Locked score: The exact score of 66 fits because responsiveness, relevance to the motion, and clarity are stronger, while evidence warrant and calibration are weaker and logical coherence remains intermediate.
